title: Explaining waiting-list growth and targeting specialty reviews
summary: I analysed 41 months of NHS waiting-times data to assess recovery, investigate renewed list growth and identify specialties needing attention. I checked the balance of pathway starts and stops, compared selected trusts and tested the planning models against a simple baseline.
scenario_note: The published data, calculations and Excel report are real. The meeting, stakeholder roles and proposed follow-up actions are simulated to show how I would handle an internal NHS performance brief. I did not work for UHB or deliver its recovery programme.
brief: During a monthly elective-performance meeting, I was asked to explain the latest waiting-time figures and identify services needing a closer review. I first established the reporting month, the pathway definitions and the decisions the report should support: monitoring recovery, investigating list growth and directing specialty-level follow-up.
requirements_intro: I used my requirements framework to separate performance reporting from capacity planning. Published totals can identify pressure and guide questions; an operational recovery plan also needs appointment capacity, cancellations, pathway stages and the reasons records leave the list.
requirements_summary: Waiting times improved substantially, but the list began growing again after March 2026. A strong position against selected peers could conceal emerging local pressure.
Has recovery continued? Do starts and stops explain the list change? Where are long waits concentrated? Which specialties are deteriorating? Are the planning models useful?
Give operational leaders a clear performance account and a focused set of specialty, data-validation and planning questions.

Consultant-led Referral to Treatment data, April 2023–August 2026; UHB, six selected Midlands trusts and England. No patient-level records, appointment-capacity data, diagnostic waits, cancer pathways or emergency care.

requirements_template.intro: These prompts show how I would agree a performance brief. The applications distinguish completed analysis, the simulated stakeholder setting and items requiring internal confirmation.

items.prompt: Who will use the report, and which decisions should it support?
items.application: The Chief Operating Officer and divisional directors need a monthly performance assessment, specialty review priorities and a qualified planning outlook. These stakeholder interactions are simulated.

items.prompt: Which population, dates and definitions make the measures interpretable?
items.application: Use incomplete pathways with known clock starts for waiting-list size and the 18-week percentage. Treat 52+ waits as pathway counts, not unique people. Compare matched April–August periods for starts and stops.

items.prompt: Which operational records would explain the aggregates, and how would access be controlled?
items.application: Request the patient tracking list, coded list adjustments and capacity data through their owners. Agree minimum fields, permissions and secure handling before using identifiable records. None are published in this case study.

items.prompt: Do record totals reconcile, and which exceptions must be explained before release?
items.application: The extraction rebuilds known-clock-start totals from weekly bands. Missing provider-month and unknown-start checks are recorded. Require a source-row check against Total All, a specialty-to-trust reconciliation and an owner-approved explanation of the stock-flow residual before operational release.

items.prompt: Which organisations form a useful benchmark, and which differences remain?
items.application: Compare UHB with six selected large Midlands acute trusts and England. Similar list sizes do not establish identical specialty mix, patient complexity or referral patterns; the ranking is descriptive.

items.prompt: Which current targets apply, and which assumptions underpin any capacity estimate?
items.application: The original pack carries March planning references from a secondary dashboard. Confirm them against official NHS guidance and local plans. Show the failed model back-test; treat the March 2027 outlook as a continuation scenario, not an agreed activity target.

items.prompt: Which outputs, deadlines and review measures would make the report usable?
items.application: Provide the workbook, a concise performance report and a review log. Agree owners, a reporting deadline, acceptance criteria and a refresh schedule. No stakeholder approval, extra clinical capacity or delivered recovery benefit is assumed.
